title: AIR Specification-First Verification Method V2
description: Reusable evidence-gated universal method for making the intended outcome and verification basis explicit before material execution, testing specification adequacy, collecting correctly classified evidence, and reconciling the result back to canonical AIR intent and acceptance criteria.

authority_boundary.operative_use_rule: Use only after exact identity and dependency validation, task-fit selection, explicit approval when required, and compilation into or explicit reference by the sole bound Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT.

purpose: Reduce execution drift and false closure across coding and non-coding work by using a proportionate intent -> specification -> verification -> evidence -> reconciliation procedure without creating a second source of truth beside canonical AIR state.

use_when: material outcome depends on correct interpretation of intent or requirements
consequence of wrong interpretation is material
evidence must justify approval, closure, publication, release, or downstream use
verification is difficult or spans multiple evidence types
work is recurrent or must transfer reliably across sessions/models/teams
research, analysis, decisions, documents, design, policy, process, or other bounded work where success can be evaluated
conditional_use: exploratory or divergent work where verification may be deferred until selection/commitment
bounded tasks where a proportionate inline SFV path is sufficient without omitting any verification, evidence, semantic-fidelity, epistemic, or gate obligation material to the promised outcome
human-evaluated outcomes where operator or reviewer evidence is the correct abstraction
do_not_use_as: a universal mandate for unit tests or TDD
a substitute for user intent or authoritative sources
a second source of truth for task center, scope, approval, or observed evidence
proof that passing verification means the intended result is correct
an execution authority independent of the current Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT

principles: Use canonical AIR task center, execution contract, acceptance criteria, ambiguity state, approval state, and evidence records as source of truth.
Define what evidence or observation would justify success before material execution when feasible.
Resolve material user-intent ambiguity through AIR-FLOOR-019-NON-INFERENCE-UNDER-MATERIAL-AMBIGUITY rather than silent inference.
Select verification according to the outcome being promised, not a preferred test technology.
Keep planned verification distinct from observed evidence.
Ask whether all planned verification could pass while the intended result is still materially wrong.
Reconcile the final result against original canonical intent and current acceptance criteria before closure.
When material uncertainty blocks verification, route the smallest sufficient clarification/evidence/source/environment requirement through RT.UNCERTAINTY_RESOLVE; do not invent missing basis.
SFV verification and cognitive outputs are candidate contributions only; Core MII fusion and the bound AIR_ARTIFACT benchmark determine operative consumption.
SFV may recommend morphology for verification nodes, but RT.MORPHOLOGY_BIND owns the binding decision.
Evidence presentation settings never reduce required verification evidence, preserved evidence, or closure criteria.

Use the smallest sufficient verification path for the promised outcome; proportionality must not omit material evidence, semantic-fidelity, epistemic-sufficiency, acceptance, alignment, gate, or closure obligations because of token cost, convenience, ceremony, task simplicity, or host preference.
inputs: current bound AIR_ARTIFACT and execution contract
canonical task center and acceptance criteria
authoritative sources or source-light limitations when material
current ambiguity, assumptions, blockers, and approval boundaries
available evidence, tools, environments, evaluators, or operator routes
domain or specialist constraints when legitimately bound

required: exactly one current Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT for material execution
AIR_GATE for material actions and closure
current acceptance criteria or explicit unresolved-intent state
required human approval when intent, binding, mutation, publication, release, or other authority is material
conditional: domain package or specialist where domain correctness requires it
EXPANDED_EVIDENCE_PRESENTATION when reviewable evidence packaging is useful; required reproducibility evidence must exist regardless of presentation mode
not_dependencies: automatic binding from upload or filename

verification_layers.purpose: Observe whether the promised user, system, document, decision, process, or research outcome is satisfied.
Check explicit promises, boundaries, rules, invariants, or states that must hold or must never occur.
Check claims against authoritative, current, and appropriately scoped sources.
Evaluate representative, boundary, exception, and failure scenarios.
Use unit, property, fixture, regression, integration, or other executable tests when they are the correct abstraction.
Verify outcomes that depend on runtime, external systems, tools, configuration, interfaces, or multiple components.
Evaluate forbidden, adversarial, unsafe, unauthorized, misuse, or failure paths when material.
Use human judgment or operator-witnessed evidence when success cannot be reduced safely to deterministic checks.
Permit task-appropriate observable evidence not captured by the standard layers.

SOFTWARE: select software verification layers according to promised behavior and risk
retain coding readiness/security/architecture review under Core coding law
RESEARCH: define research question and decision-use boundary
test contrary evidence and unresolved gaps
reconcile findings to the original question rather than source volume
ANALYSIS_DECISION: evaluate scenarios, alternatives, counterexamples, and sensitivity
reconcile recommendation to original decision need
DOCUMENT_COMMUNICATION: define audience, purpose, required content, constraints, and source fidelity
verify completeness, factual support, internal coherence, and delivery format
use human review where tone or persuasive quality is material
DESIGN_UX: define intended user-visible outcome and constraints
verify interaction states, accessibility, comprehension, and representative user paths
use human evaluation when aesthetic or experiential judgment is material
POLICY_PROCESS: define rule/process outcome, scope, exceptions, actors, and escalation paths
verify scenario coverage, conflicts, exceptions, and operational feasibility
preserve human authority where policy decisions are non-transferable
EXPLORATORY: allow incomplete verification while experimental status is explicit
do not infer readiness, approval, or closure from exploration
OTHER: map canonical intent and acceptance criteria
choose observable evidence appropriate to the task

ordered_steps.name: SPECIFICATION_TARGET_AND_TASK_CLASSIFICATION
ordered_steps.action: Resolve references to the canonical AIR intent, goal, scope, acceptance criteria, and task class without creating a duplicate intent source.
preconditions: current task exists at least in preliminary form
required_inputs: bound artifact or candidate specification state
evidence_to_advance: canonical specification sources are identified
materially unknown intent is visible
method-local state does not replace canonical AIR state
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when the intended outcome cannot be distinguished from an assumption or the canonical target is materially unresolved.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-02 when the specification target is sufficiently explicit.

ordered_steps.name: OUTCOME_AND_BOUNDARY_MODEL
ordered_steps.action: Map success, boundaries, material failure/exception states, and domain-specific realization against canonical acceptance criteria.
evidence_to_advance: material success and failure/exception semantics have been considered
model references canonical criteria instead of creating a second source of truth
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when verification cannot yet distinguish satisfactory from materially wrong outcomes.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-03 after a reviewable outcome/boundary model exists.

ordered_steps.name: AMBIGUITY_AND_UNCERTAINTY_CHALLENGE
ordered_steps.action: Identify materially different interpretations, hidden assumptions, missing authoritative evidence, and underspecified failure semantics.
evidence_to_advance: material user-intent ambiguity is resolved by the authorized human or explicitly blocked
externally verifiable uncertainty is evidenced or correctly gated
no material ambiguity is converted into an operative assumption
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW for unresolved user-controlled ambiguity; EVIDENCE_REQUIRED for missing required authoritative evidence; route the smallest sufficient missing input through RT.UNCERTAINTY_RESOLVE and AIR_REQUIRED_INPUT_REQUEST when the basis gap is material.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-04 when remaining ambiguity is non-material, explicitly unresolved without affecting the step, or safely gated.

ordered_steps.name: VERIFICATION_STRATEGY_SELECTION
ordered_steps.action: Select the smallest sufficient combination of observable verification layers appropriate to the promised outcome, risks, sources, and domain.
preconditions: blocking ambiguity for the affected step is resolved or gated
evidence_to_advance: each selected layer maps to an intended outcome, constraint, or risk
technology-specific tests are not selected merely by habit
human/operator/source evidence is selected when it is the correct abstraction
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when the chosen verification cannot establish the promised outcome.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-05 when the verification strategy fits the canonical specification.

ordered_steps.name: VERIFICATION_SPECIFICATION
ordered_steps.action: Define planned checks, observations, scenarios, source comparisons, evaluations, fixtures, tests, or operator reviews and their expected results before execution when feasible.
evidence_to_advance: verification items map back to canonical specification targets
expected results are stated before observation when feasible
planned verification is clearly distinguished from observed evidence
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when verification primarily encodes an anticipated solution instead of the intended outcome.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-06 when verification is concrete enough to judge adequacy.

ordered_steps.name: SPECIFICATION_ADEQUACY_GATE
ordered_steps.action: Ask whether every proposed verification item could pass while the intended result is still materially wrong.
evidence_to_advance: each material intended outcome has a verification path or explicit justified exception
material failure/exception semantics are represented
a positive verification result would constitute meaningful evidence for the current specification
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW for resolvable adequacy gaps; EVIDENCE_REQUIRED when design depends on unavailable information; REJECT when verification contradicts the intended outcome; RESCOPE_REQUIRED when resolution changes task center or criteria.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-07 only when method_step_gate is ALLOW.

ordered_steps.name: PREEXECUTION_BASELINE
ordered_steps.action: When useful, establish a reference state showing that the selected verification can distinguish current/pre-change state from the intended state.
required_inputs: current state or reference state when available
evidence_to_advance: baseline is established when it materially improves discrimination
inability to establish a baseline is explicit rather than fabricated
baseline evidence is correctly classified
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: EVIDENCE_REQUIRED when a required baseline cannot be obtained; REVIEW when baseline contradicts the specification.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-08 after sufficient baseline evidence exists or a justified non-baseline route is recorded.

ordered_steps.name: EXECUTION_HANDOFF
ordered_steps.action: Prepare an execution-handoff candidate only under the current bound AIR artifact, current verification specification, current approvals and AIR_GATE. SFV does not itself authorize RT.ACTION.
preconditions: baseline condition satisfied or justifiably omitted
current Orbit 0 AIR artifact is bound with an ACTIVE lease, matching resource scope pin when material, current approval, and AIR_GATE ALLOW for the exact proposed effect
evidence_to_advance: execution scope matches the canonical specification
no new material outcome is silently introduced
a matching single-use AIR_ACTION_AUTHORIZATION exists before material mutation or external action and authorizes exactly one declared effect attempt
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: BLOCKED_BY_CONTRACT or RESCOPE_REQUIRED when execution would exceed the active contract.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Execution may proceed only through Core RT.ACTION when the bound artifact, ACTIVE lease, matching scope pin, current approval, method_step_gate, and AIR_GATE permit the exact effect; after any material effect attempt, post-effect alignment and Core RT.RECEIPT / AIR_ACTION_RECEIPT are required before dependent action, delivery, or closure. SFV handoff is candidate input, not authorization.

ordered_steps.name: VERIFICATION_EXECUTION
ordered_steps.action: Run, obtain, or observe the selected verification evidence and compare observations with the predeclared expectations.
preconditions: required evidence route exists and any material effect has a matching single-use authorization plus reconciled Core RT.RECEIPT / AIR_ACTION_RECEIPT before dependent action or closure
evidence_to_advance: results are tool-observed, operator-witnessed, source-supported, human-reviewed, replayable, or otherwise correctly classified
planned and observed evidence remain distinct
material failures remain visible
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW on resolvable failures; EVIDENCE_REQUIRED when required evidence is unavailable; REJECT when required outcome fails and no permitted remediation remains.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-10 only after required verification passes or an explicit AIR-approved remediation route exists.

ordered_steps.name: INTEGRITY_REVIEW
ordered_steps.action: Review the result for task-appropriate integrity beyond the narrow verification set, including coherence, source fidelity, architecture/security, constraint preservation, quality, or downstream compatibility as applicable.
preconditions: required verification has completed sufficiently for review
evidence_to_advance: verified outcomes remain intact after any corrections
material constraints and risk obligations remain satisfied or visibly unresolved
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when integrity review exposes resolvable defects; EVIDENCE_REQUIRED when required evidence is missing.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Advance to SFV-11 after integrity state is acceptable for closure review.

ordered_steps.name: INTENT_RECONCILIATION_AND_CLOSURE
ordered_steps.action: Compare the verified result back to the original canonical AIR intent and current acceptance criteria instead of closing solely because selected verification passed.
preconditions: verification execution and integrity review completed as required
evidence_to_advance: original intended outcome remains represented
no material requirement was lost through verification shaping
unrepresented/newly discovered outcomes are explicitly handled
AIR closure evidence requirements are satisfied
ordered_steps.failure_behavior: REVIEW when verification passes but intent reconciliation fails; RESCOPE_REQUIRED when discovered intent materially changes the task; REJECT when required outcome remains unsatisfied.
ordered_steps.next_step_rule: Method may recommend COMPLETE only when reconciliation supports closure; RT.DELIVER and RT.CLOSE remain Core-owned and require applicable AIR_GATE/dependencies.

stale_when: bound method scope or domain realization changes materially
Core NEW_TASK_BOUNDARY is detected, Orbit 0 task identity changes, or a different task AIR_ARTIFACT becomes bound
recovery: return to the earliest affected method step
preserve unaffected evidence only where applicability remains demonstrable
rerun specification adequacy before affected execution resumes
treat prior-task SFV state as historical or candidate input until applicability is revalidated under the newly bound task AIR_ARTIFACT

handoff_requirements: method_specific_state containing specification_target_refs, task_classification, open ambiguity/assumption/evidence requests, selected verification layers, verification_specification identity/content or canonical reference, specification adequacy decision, baseline evidence state, observed verification evidence refs, integrity review state, intent reconciliation state, and test_evidence_mode when material

binding_requirements.responsive_approval_rule: A direct exact upload may satisfy explicit user binding approval only when Core opened a pre-disclosed responsive binding gate naming this exact pack, scope, effects, and excluded effects. Validation and binding remain separate.
binding_requirements.orbit_rule: The Method Pack never becomes Orbit 0 and never independently grants execution authority. Applicable method requirements become operative only when compiled into or explicitly referenced by the current active AIR_ARTIFACT.
binding_requirements.gate_rule: Use the stricter practical result when method_step_gate and AIR_GATE differ.
binding_requirements.floor_rule: The Method Pack may tighten but never relax AIR floor invariants.
binding_requirements.new_task_boundary_rule: A Core NEW_TASK_BOUNDARY or change of Orbit 0 task identity invalidates operative carryover of prior-task SFV method state. The new task must use its newly bound AIR_ARTIFACT; prior SFV specification, verification, and evidence may be reused only after explicit applicability revalidation.

method_gate_contract.state_boundary: EVIDENCE_REQUIRED and RESCOPE_REQUIRED are gate decisions, not method-step states.
method_gate_contract.air_gate_precedence: AIR_GATE controls material task action and closure. method_step_gate is an input; the stricter practical consequence governs.

claim_boundary.supported_claim: This Method Pack defines a reusable universal AIR procedure for specification-first verification across task classes with domain-specific realizations.
unsupported_without_empirical_evidence: that it reduces defects or errors
that it is superior to TDD or another method
that it improves product-market fit or decision quality
that it guarantees correct requirements or intent
that passing its verification proves production readiness, compliance, safety, or truth

required_checks: all ordered steps contain required step fields
method never grants Orbit 0 authority independently
canonical_state_mapping prevents duplicate task-intent, scope, approval, or observed-evidence authority
planned verification is distinct from observed evidence
unit testing and TDD are not mandatory universal first layers
responsive upload can satisfy approval only through a pre-disclosed Core/Governance binding gate
final intent reconciliation is required before closure of material method-governed work

software_realization.behavior_specification_required_when: coding changes externally observable behavior, contracts, state transitions, security boundaries, or defect outcomes
rules: unit testing is not the universal first layer
security-sensitive work requires negative/abuse coverage where material
schema/configuration may use fixtures/invariants/compatibility instead of conventional unit tests

required_input_acquisition_contract.behavior: Check the current session and validated package inventory first; request the smallest exact missing component, source, tool, environment, evaluator, approval, clarification, or action; request the complete five-file SFV package when coupled use or package validation is required.
required_input_acquisition_contract.attachment_boundary: Receipt establishes availability only, not selection, approval, binding, execution, verification, or closure authority.

integration_refresh.optional_hash_policy: Do not pin optional peer-package manifest hashes inside mutually compatible package bytes. Validate exact manifest identity, hash, version, dependencies and task fit at selection time to avoid cyclic hash invalidation.

mii_sfv_contribution_contract.fusion_boundary: SFV may identify evidence support/conflict edges, verification gaps and intent-reconciliation candidates, but Core MII owns cognitive contribution fusion and the AIR_ARTIFACT benchmark owns operative consumption.
mii_sfv_contribution_contract.authority_boundary: No SFV cognitive contribution, verification result, adequacy recommendation or specialist decision independently authorizes execution, material action, delivery, closure, approval, binding or Orbit 0 occupancy.

semantic_fidelity_contract.sfv_rule: SFV derives verification targets from resolved canonical intent, active context, acceptance criteria and authoritative source state. Verification shaping may not silently replace, narrow, broaden or reinterpret material intent.
semantic_fidelity_contract.closure_rule: Passing selected verification is insufficient for closure unless the verified result reconciles back to canonical intent, active context and current acceptance criteria through Core delivery/closure routes.
semantic_fidelity_contract.raw_input_boundary: A verification specification, translated requirement or intent-reconciliation candidate never supersedes raw user input as evidence of what the user actually said.

epistemic_sufficiency_contract.sfv_role: Identify missing specification basis, authoritative evidence, environment state, evaluator evidence or user-controlled ambiguity and propose the smallest sufficient missing input.
epistemic_sufficiency_contract.non_inference_rule: Material uncertainty is not converted into an operative assumption merely to complete a verification path.
epistemic_sufficiency_contract.continuation_rule: Continue only where the unresolved uncertainty is non-material to the affected verification target or is explicitly gated without weakening acceptance criteria.

morphology_contribution_contract.observable_effect_requirement: Every morphology recommendation must state the verification objective and observable effect on decomposition, coverage, pruning or review. Labels without observable effect are UNBOUND_DECORATIVE.
morphology_contribution_contract.claim_boundary: SFV may not claim direct latent-space control, measured internal model effect, or BACKEND_BOUND morphology without evidence.

test_evidence_contract.presentation_only_rule: The -t modifier controls evidence presentation and packaging only. It does not reduce evidence acquisition requirements, preservation, verification coverage, cognitive work, benchmark rigor, review obligations, acceptance criteria or closure requirements.
test_evidence_contract.standard_presentation_rule: Show the verification decision, scoped counts or states, evidence classes, material failures, limitations and sufficient evidence references without omitting evidence needed to justify the result.
test_evidence_contract.expanded_presentation_rule: Surface available reviewable test/evaluation artifacts and references when they exist and may be disclosed.
test_evidence_contract.retroactivity_rule: Presentation mode may reveal already preserved evidence but must not fabricate missing historical evidence. A new authorized run is required when evidence itself is missing for an applicable acceptance, regulatory or reproducibility obligation.
test_evidence_contract.rights_and_reasoning_boundary: Do not expose hidden reasoning, private chain of thought, secrets, credentials, restricted source text or unavailable backend logs.

core_route_ownership.sfv_effect: SFV supplies candidate verification strategy, cognitive/evidence contributions, adequacy findings, observed verification results and closure recommendations. It does not create parallel Core routes or positive execution authority.

alignment_evaluation_dependency.relationship: Any formal AIR object that incorporates SFV output must satisfy the current Core evaluation-basis constructor dependency. SFV candidate records are not a bypass.

mii_contribution_authority.operative_rule: SFV Domain, Method, Specialist and Executor outputs become operative only after validation and compilation into or explicit reference by the sole bound Orbit 0 AIR_ARTIFACT.execution_benchmark_profile.

capability_ecology_peer.note: Observed T7 candidate identity is validation evidence for T9 only; runtime selection validates the then-supplied exact package.

grounding_peer.note: Observed T8 candidate identity is validation evidence for T9 only; runtime selection validates the then-supplied exact package.
